Front page Music. The music of rising pop star Stemin: “The Weeknd but make it gay”
Music.

The music of rising pop star Stemin: “The Weeknd but make it gay”

This article is sponsored.
© Mimi van Amerongen

Your timeline is disappearing. This newspaper remains. Receive De Regulist in print every quarter.

View the subscriptions

“The Weeknd, but gay,” is how Stemin describes his own music.
The Amsterdam pop artist is releasing his very first single on May 30. With ambiguous lyrics and funky sounds, Stemin takes you into his personal experiences as a queer man.

“As a Swiss-born person, raised in conservative Italian culture, I used to find it difficult to talk about topics like sex and sexuality,” the singer says. Nowadays, things are quite different. In his songs, Stemin openly describes the sexual experiences he has had over the past few years. “It is actually a kind of coming-of-age story. Very raw and honest. I lay bare my entire process; from prudishness to who I am now.”

Stemin's music is certainly not falling on deaf ears. He previously performed on the main stage at Dam Square during Pride Amsterdam. This summer, the pop artist will once again take to various stages. He kicks things off with his own release party: “On June 14th, Cinetol is the place to be in Amsterdam. It’s going to be a huge party, and I encourage everyone to come!” says Stemin enthusiastically.

However, that is not the only plus for the Swiss artist in a short time. “I recently joined the label Amber Music. That is not only incredibly cool, but it also means that my music will be easy to find on all streaming platforms from now on.”

Is there a deeper layer to his ambiguous lyrics? Absolutely! “Remember: you always come back to yourself. Only by being yourself can we, as a community, survive in this society.”

Listen to Stemin's newest single starting May 30, available on your favorite streaming platform! Tickets to the release party can be found here .
